standard.title: Guide for Determining Compatibility Between Enamelled Winding Wire and Impregnating Compounds (इनेमल्ड वाइंडिंग वायर और संसेचन यौगिकों के बीच संगतता निर्धारण हेतु मार्गदर्शिका)
standard.sector: Electrotechnical / Solid Electrical Insulating Materials and Insulation Systems
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes technical guidelines and pre-selection test methodologies to determine the relative chemical compatibility between enamelled round winding wires and impregnating compounds (such as solventless resins and impregnating varnishes) used in the insulation systems of electrical rotating and static machines.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes technical guidelines and pre-selection test methodologies to determine the relative chemical compatibility between enamelled round winding wires and impregnating compounds (such as solventless resins and impregnating varnishes) used in the insulation systems of electrical rotating and static machines.

supersedes: None (Developed as a new standalone guide to govern pre-selection evaluations of wire-varnish insulation interfaces)

certification.description: Voluntary National Code. However, under public works specifications, defense procurement, railway traction motor guidelines, and heavy industrial machinery tenders, motor manufacturers must supply type-approval certificates certifying that the wire enamel and impregnating varnish combination has successfully completed compatibility testing per IS 14353.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, temperature values, and dielectric breakdown voltages must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in this standard.

The majority of electrical winding difficulties arise when an enamelled wire is used in combination with an impregnating compound that causes a chemical reaction between the cured enamelled film and the compound, which is accelerated by high temperatures and degrades wire electrical/mechanical properties.

Twisted pair ageing is confirmed by extensive experience in India and globally. It evaluates changes in dielectric breakdown voltage (BDV) of impregnated enamelled twisted-pair specimens after exposure to accelerated thermal ageing.

Twisted-pair specimens (prepared per IS 13778 Part 5) are pre-heated for 10 minutes at 130°C, cooled for 1 hour, immersed in the impregnant for 10 minutes, and withdrawn at 10 cm/min prior to standard curing.

Ageing is conducted inside an air-circulated electric oven for 168 hours (Set G1) or 336 hours (Set G2) at an ageing temperature T selected according to the temperature class of the wire and varnish, raised by 40°C (e.g. for Class 155, T = 195°C). Set G0 serves as the unaged control.
Twisted pair cyclic ageing is less established, with insufficient technical experience available. Due to this, the standard does not include end-point evaluation criteria for Method B.

The guide does not cover rectangular wires or fibrous-covered conductors. It is by no means a method to test the complete insulation system of an electrical machine, as environmental factors (humidity, chemical contamination, mechanical vibration, etc.) are excluded and must be verified separately (e.g. via motorette testing).
